class.name: CbItem
class.brief_description: Makes a scene an item: the root of the item's own scene says which kind it is, what it is called and what it weighs.
class.description: One scene is one item. Its root is a [CbItem]; everything under it is the item: - a [CollisionShape3D] with a [BoxShape3D] or a [SphereShape3D]: its body when it lies in the world, placed where the shape's centre is. It may be turned any way, but not scaled. - two markers ([Marker3D]) that [member carry_grip] and [member other_grip] name: where the hands hold it. - meshes, lights, particles: how it looks in the hand, put away and on the floor. - [CbReaction] nodes: what it shows when its holder does something (a muzzle flash). The scene is the item's frame: the grip at the origin, pointing along -Z. The root's own transform is not used. Saving the scene bakes [code]res://items/<kind>.cfg[/code] (the Bake button and publishing the mod do too). The server reads the body, the grip and the [member properties] from that file in the mod's workshop item; the game finds the scene, the [member display_name] and the first-person settings (the [code]view_[/code] members) by it. A server mod declares the kind ([code]declare.ItemKind( "melee.bat" )[/code]) and says what it does. In the game the node does nothing: the simulation owns the item.

method.name: bake
method.description: The text of [code]items/<kind>.cfg[/code]: [code]{ text, error }[/code] ([code]text[/code] is empty when the item cannot be baked, and [code]error[/code] says why).

method.name: bake_to_project
method.description: What the Bake button and saving the scene do: writes [code]res://items/<kind>.cfg[/code], only when its bytes change. Servers get it when the mod is published.

members.member: The socket the item hangs in while it is put away ([code]Hip[/code], [code]Back[/code]); empty: out of sight. Read by a server mod that takes its items from its look.
The kind this scene is, in one word: the name a server mod declares ([code]melee.bat[/code]). The baked file is named after it, and a project has one scene per kind.
What prompts and lists call it ([code]Bat[/code]): [code]{look:field}[/code] and an item's [code]{name}[/code] in a format. Empty: its kind.
What it weighs when it lies in the world, in kilograms.

Its own state: a field of every copy of the item ([code]{"gun.rounds": 12}[/code]). The scene declares it; a new copy starts with the value and keeps its own from then on, as simulation state (predicted, rolled back, in a joining player's snapshot). The value's type is the field's: a whole number an Int, a decimal a Float, [code]true[/code] / [code]false[/code] a Bool. Server mods read and write it ([code]ctx.Get[/code] / [code]ctx.Set[/code] on the item's NetId); looks read the one in a player's hand as [code]hand.<field>[/code] ([code]{hand.gun.rounds}[/code]).
Named numbers any server mod may read: [code]pickup.hold_seconds[/code] = 0.5, [code]inventory.slot[/code] = 3. They replace what the item's mod declared in code for the same names.

How long a use of it lasts, on a server with slots. Any copy is used from the hand (its slot's key takes it out, the left mouse button uses it), or by its own [member use_key] wherever it is carried. [b]While the button is down[/b]: a tool, a weapon. [b]Once a press[/b]: an ability, a consumable (the grenade, the dash boots, the grappling hook). [b]A press, and while held[/b]: in use as long as the button or key is down (a jetpack). Whichever way, its server mod is told the same thing ([code]ctx.Used[/code], [code]ctx.Using[/code], [code]ctx.UsedItem[/code]: which copy), conditions read [code]using.<kind>[/code], and the simulation records the event [code]<kind>.used[/code] on the press (declared for an item of a mod that takes its items from its look), so a [CbMotion] or a [CbReaction] on it starts at once on the player's own screen.

With [member preview_hold]: the event the Fire the cue button fires ([code]melee.swing[/code]). It plays on the figure and in the First person panel: the pack's state machine hears it (a state entered on it, or on a stance a [CbPrediction] of this scene sets with it), and the item in the hand, a whole copy of this scene, plays its [CbReaction] nodes. The mod's [code]vfx/reactions*.tscn[/code] play beside the figure too.

In the editor: shows the item in a hand. A stand-in figure (the SDK skeleton's bones, as boxes) stands a metre beside the item and holds a copy of it by [member carry_grip], in the pose of a baked animation pack of this project, with its other hand where [member other_hand] and [member other_grip] put it. It is posed by the code that poses players in the game. Move a grip marker and the copy in the hand follows (within half a second). While it is on, a First person panel beside the 3D view shows what the holder sees, with [member view_offset], [member view_rotation], [member view_fov] and the hands applied as the game applies them. Not saved.
With [member preview_hold]: the carrying arm is aimed level, as it is for an item whose mod makes the holder face the camera (a gun).
The pack [member preview_hold] plays (a folder of [code]res://anim[/code], such as [code]melee.hold[/code]); empty: the item's own [member animation_pack], or the first there is.
When used: fields of the player a use changes ([code]dash.charges -= 1[/code]). For the motion nodes under the item (what using it does).

When used: expressions that must all hold for a use to do anything ([code]dash.charges > 0[/code]). The motion nodes under the item ([CbProbe], [CbLink], [CbForce], [CbImpulse], [CbLaunch], [CbMove]) are what a use does; they bake with the item into one motion named [code]Use[/code].
When used: seconds between two uses.
When used: the event a use says ([code]dash.started[/code]), at the player: for looks and state machines.

Its own key ([code]H[/code], [code]MouseRight[/code]): uses the first copy the player carries (the selected one, else the lowest slot's) where it is, without taking it out. It is the mod action [code]<kind>.use[/code] ([code]{key:frag.grenade.use}[/code] in a HUD); the player's own choice (the Keys page of the settings) wins. Empty: it is used from the hand only.
What it looks like in an inventory's slot (a [CbItemIcon] shows it). None: the game takes a picture of this scene once (its meshes, framed, from the front and a little above) and uses that.

How many of it one slot holds: a stack (1: one). An item given to a player who has a stack of its kind with room goes onto it (as many as fit; the rest goes on as an item of its own); a [CbLaunch] of the one carried throws one off the stack, with the stack's fields, and the rest stays. The HUD reads the count as [code]slot.count[/code]; server mods as [code]CarriedItem::count[/code].

Thrown fast and small (a dart, a rocket): in the world it is moved with continuous collision against what moves too (a crate, a door), so it does not pass a thin one between two steps. The level's walls stop anything without it. It costs a little more each step.

Which hand it is in. [constant HAND_SELECTED]: the slots' hand, while its slot is the selected one. [constant HAND_LEFT]: the left hand for as long as it is carried, beside what the slots' hand holds (a torch beside a gun). It is put away while what is selected has its other hand at a marker (a rifle's barrel), or while another such item of a lower slot is there; what has its other hand as the animation has it (a pistol, a bat) is held with one hand beside it.

The slot it goes to when a player comes to carry one (1 is the first), if that one is free; else, or with 0, the first free slot. Nothing is pushed out: a slot is a place, and a second copy goes to another one.

The animation pack the item brings ([code]gun.pistol_hold[/code]: a [CbAnimPack] scene of this project, by its name): while one is held, the pack's layers play instead of the holder's own. Empty: the character's own animations. Read by a server mod that takes its items from its look ([code]declare.ItemsOfLook()[/code]).

The marker the item is carried at: this point is in the hand's socket (whichever hand the item is in), its -Z along the fingers and +Y up. Move or turn the marker, not the model: a mesh imported with its origin anywhere is held where this is. Empty: the item is carried at its scene's origin.
What the character's other hand does while it is empty.
The marker the other hand is held at, for [constant OTHER_AT_MARKER] and [constant OTHER_AT_MARKER_TURNED].

First person, the other way: a node in the scene that stands where the viewer's eye is while this is held (a [CbViewCamera]: tick its Preview to place the item by looking). With one, the item does not follow the body's animation in its holder's view: the camera holds it, the arms are bent onto its grips, and its animation there is its own (an [AnimationPlayer] moving the meshes and the grip markers, played by a [CbReaction] with the condition [code]first_person[/code]). [member view_offset] and [member view_rotation] are not used then. Empty (the usual): the view shows the body's own animation.

First person: the field of view the arms and the item are drawn with, in degrees. They are drawn apart from the world, over it, so this does not change the world's picture. Less than 60 makes them flatter and smaller. 0: the game's own (60).
First person: whether the left arm is drawn while this is held.

First person: how far the hands and the item are moved in the holder's own view from where the animation has them, in metres to the right, up and ahead. The arms reach from shoulders that stay; a hand out of reach stays at the arm's length. The animation itself is the one everyone sees: a hold made for third person is usually low and out of the picture, and this brings it in.
First person: whether the right arm is drawn while this is held.
First person: how the item is turned in the holder's own view, about the carrying hand, in degrees: x tips it up, y turns it to the left, z rolls it. The hands turn with it.

constants.constant: In the slots' hand, while its slot is the selected one.
In the left hand for as long as it is carried, when that hand is free.
In use while the button (or its own key) is down; one press is one use. A tool, a weapon.
One use a press, however long it is held. A consumable, an ability.
The animation's: nothing keeps it on the item. A one-handed item.
The other arm is bent so that its wrist is at [member other_grip], wherever the carrying hand and the animation take the item. The hand keeps the turn its animation gives it.
The same, and the hand is turned as the marker is: as a hand carrying an item placed there would be.

The hand stays where the item's animations have it relative to the carrying hand, place and turn; no marker. For animations made with both hands on the item: they are kept as they are, and kept together when the carrying arm is aimed up or down.
